title: 第九章 派出所的问询第十章 临时的身份证明
lines: 第九章派出所的问询
初秋的午后，阳光透过百叶窗在派出所接待室的地板上投下斑驳的光影。凌峰坐在硬塑料椅上，指尖无意识地摩挲着裤缝。身旁的刘佳琪微微侧着头，目光落在墙上“严肃执法，热情服务”的标语上，长长的睫毛轻轻颤动着，藏不住眼底的紧张。
接待他们的是一位年轻的民警，姓王，胸前的警号在白炽灯下泛着冷光。他刚给两人倒了杯温水，此刻正低头翻看着桌上的登记表，笔尖在纸页上停顿片刻，抬起头看向凌峰：“再确认一下，你们俩是昨天傍晚在佘山北麓附近迷路，今天早上才找到下山的路？”
“是。”凌峰的声音有些干涩，他清了清嗓子，尽量让语气听起来自然，“我们本来是去爬山看日落，没想到走错了路，山里信号不好，手机也没带够电，就……被困了一晚上。”
这个说辞是他们在路上反复斟酌过的。从穿越过来的那一刻起，凌峰就意识到，暴露“时空来客”的身份绝对是下下策。眼前的世界陌生得让人脊背发凉——空中掠过的梭型飞行器、路面上无声滑行的交通工具、还有那些穿着他从未见过的制服、配备着奇特装备的巡逻人员……这一切都在提醒他，他们闯入了一个不属于自己的时代。谨慎，是眼下唯一的生存法则。
王警官点点头，在表格上划了个勾，又看向刘佳琪：“刘女士，你是凌先生的妻子？你们的户籍地……”他顿了顿，眉头微蹙，“登记表上写的是‘原住地信息暂无法提供’，这是什么情况？”
刘佳琪捏着水杯的手指紧了紧，杯壁上的水珠顺着指缝滑落在手背上，带来一丝冰凉的触感。她深吸一口气，按照事先商量好的话说：“我们……我们之前一直在外地做点小生意，住的是临时的出租屋，后来搬了几次家，户口本和身份证不小心在搬家的时候弄丢了。本想着回上海补办，结果刚到这边就出了这档子事。”
她说得半真半假。他们的确是“回”上海——只是这个“回”，回的是九十年后的上海。至于身份证和户口本，在他们原来的世界里好好收在家里的抽屉里，可在这里，自然是“丢失”了。
王警官的目光在两人脸上转了一圈，没说话，起身拿起桌上的扫描仪。“麻烦二位配合一下，先做个身份核验。”他将扫描仪对准凌峰的额头，一道微弱的绿光扫过，仪器屏幕上瞬间跳出一串代码，紧接着弹出一行红色的提示：“无匹配身份信息”。
同样的操作在刘佳琪身上重复了一遍，结果如出一辙。
王警官放下扫描仪，脸上的表情严肃了几分：“系统里查不到你们的任何信息。没有户籍登记，没有社保记录，没有交通出行痕迹……二位，这可不是小事。”
凌峰的心猛地一沉。他早料到这个时代的身份系统会很严格，却没想到严格到这种地步。在他们生活的年代，身份信息虽然重要，但总有漏洞可钻，可眼前这台小小的仪器，似乎能将一个人从出生到现在的轨迹都扒得一干二净。
“警官，我们真的是证件丢了。”凌峰的语气带着恳切，“我们在外地待了快十年，一直在小地方打转，没怎么用过这些电子设备，可能……可能系统里本来就没什么记录？”他努力回忆着昨天在路上看到的那些“方块”——邻居张阿姨后来告诉他们那叫“个人终端”，似乎人人都离不开。他猜测，这个时代的人大概很少有像他们这样“脱离系统”的。
王警官没立刻回应，他调出了两人的面部识别档案，放大在屏幕上。凌峰的脸棱角分明，眉宇间带着几分沉稳，只是眼下的青黑暴露了他一夜未眠的疲惫；刘佳琪的面容清秀，眼神里带着一丝不易察觉的警惕，却并不像是作奸犯科之人。
“你们说在外地做小生意，具体是做什么的？”王警官的声音放缓了些，“在哪里做的？有认识的人可以证明吗？”
“开了家中餐厅。”凌峰答得很快，这是他最熟悉的领域，“在……在南方一个小县城，叫溪口。那边熟人不少，但我们这几年没怎么联系，突然找过去，怕人家也记不清了。”他故意说了个偏远的地名，赌对方不会立刻去核实。
王警官指尖在键盘上敲了敲，屏幕上跳出溪口县的相关信息。他看了几秒，抬眼道：“溪口县五年前就完成了全员电子身份登记，就算你们十年前离开，系统里也该有原始户籍存档。但现在，你们的信息是完全空白的，就像……”他顿了顿，没说下去，但那眼神里的探究已经很明显了。
刘佳琪的心提到了嗓子眼，她下意识地攥住了凌峰的手。凌峰感受到她掌心的冰凉，轻轻回握了一下，示意她别慌。他知道，一味强调“证件丢失”已经站不住脚了，必须想个更合理的解释。
“警官，”凌峰的语气沉了沉，像是下定了某种决心，“不瞒您说，我们这十年过得不太顺。中间遇到点事，跟家里断了联系，后来又换了好几份工作，住的地方也不固定，连原来的名字都快忘了……这次来上海，就是想重新开始，没想到刚到就迷了路。”他故意说得含糊，把“丢失证件”的原因引向“与社会脱节”，试图用一种落魄感来解释信息空白的异常。
这番话半真半假，却恰好戳中了某些可能存在的社会现象。王警官的眉头舒展了些许，他见过不少因逃避债务、家庭矛盾而故意“消失”的人，虽然眼前这两人看起来不像，但也不能完全排除这种可能。
他沉默了片刻，起身道：“你们先在这儿等一下，我去跟领导汇报一下情况。”
办公室的门被轻轻带上，接待室里只剩下凌峰和刘佳琪两人。空气仿佛凝固了，只有墙上的电子钟在无声地跳动着，每一秒都像敲在心上。
“阿峰，”刘佳琪的声音压得很低，带着颤抖，“他们会不会……怀疑我们？”
凌峰握住她的手，指尖的温度传递过去：“别担心，我们没做错事，只是身份特殊了点。他们最多觉得我们是失联人口，不会往别的地方想的。”话虽如此，他心里也没底。这个时代的警察，会不会有更敏锐的直觉？他们的言行举止，有没有露出什么破绽？

Chapter 9 Inquiries at the Police Station
On an early autumn afternoon, the sun shines through the blinds, casting mottled light and shadow on the floor of the reception room of the police station. Ling Feng sat on the hard plastic chair, his fingertips unconsciously rubbing the seam of his trousers. Liu Jiaqi beside her tilted her head slightly, her eyes falling on the slogan "Serious Law Enforcement, Enthusiastic Service" on the wall. Her long eyelashes trembled slightly, unable to hide the tension in her eyes.
The person who received them was a young policeman named Wang. The police signal on his chest glowed coldly under the incandescent lamp. He had just poured a glass of warm water for the two of them, and was now looking down at the registration form on the table. The pen tip paused on the page for a moment, then raised his head and looked at Ling Feng: "Just to confirm, you two got lost near the northern foot of Sheshan Mountain last evening and only found the way down the mountain this morning?"
"Yes." Ling Feng's voice was a little dry. He cleared his throat and tried to sound natural. "We originally went to climb the mountain to watch the sunset. Unexpectedly, we took the wrong road. The signal in the mountain was not good, and the mobile phone did not have enough battery, so... we were trapped all night."
This argument was something they considered over and over again on the road. From the moment he traveled through time and space, Ling Feng realized that exposing the identity of the "time and space visitor" was definitely a bad idea. The world in front of him was so strange that it sent chills down the spine - the shuttle aircraft passing by in the sky, the vehicles gliding silently on the road, and the patrol officers wearing uniforms and strange equipment that he had never seen before... all of these reminded him that they had entered an era that did not belong to their own. Caution is the only rule of survival right now.
Officer Wang nodded, checked the form, and then looked at Liu Jiaqi: "Ms. Liu, are you Mr. Ling's wife? Your place of residence..." He paused and frowned, "The registration form says 'the information of the place of origin cannot be provided temporarily'. What's going on?"
Liu Jiaqi squeezed the water glass tightly with her fingers, and the water drops on the wall of the glass slid down between her fingers and fell on the back of her hand, bringing a cold touch. She took a deep breath and followed the pre-arranged words: "We...we had been doing a small business out of town and lived in a temporary rental house. Later, we moved several times. We accidentally lost our household registration book and ID card when we moved. I wanted to go back to Shanghai to replace them, but something like this happened as soon as I arrived here."
She told half-truths. They are indeed "returning" to Shanghai - but this "return" is to Shanghai ninety years later. As for their ID cards and household registration books, they were kept in drawers at home in their original world, but here they were naturally "lost".
Officer Wang's eyes moved around the faces of the two people, without saying anything, he stood up and picked up the scanner on the table. "Please cooperate with me and do an identity verification first." He pointed the scanner at Ling Feng's forehead, and a faint green light swept across it. A string of codes instantly popped up on the screen of the instrument, followed by a line of red prompts: "No matching identity information."
The same operation was repeated on Liu Jiaqi, with the same result.
Officer Wang put down the scanner, with a serious expression on his face: "No information about you can be found in the system. There is no household registration, no social security records, no traces of traffic... You two, this is no small matter."
Ling Feng's heart suddenly sank. He had expected that the identity system in this era would be very strict, but he did not expect it to be so strict. In the era they lived in, although identity information was important, there were always loopholes to exploit, but this small instrument in front of them seemed to be able to trace a person's trajectory from birth to the present.
"Officer, we really lost our documents." Ling Feng's tone was sincere. "We have been out in the field for almost ten years and have been wandering around in small places. We have not used these electronic devices very much. Maybe... maybe there are no records in the system?" He tried hard to recall the "squares" he saw on the road yesterday - his neighbor Aunt Zhang later told them that they were called "personal terminals", and it seemed that everyone could not live without them. He guessed that there were probably very few people in this era who were as "out of the system" as they were.
Officer Wang didn't respond immediately. He called up the facial recognition files of the two people and zoomed in on the screen. Ling Feng's face had sharp edges and corners, and there was a certain calmness between his brows, but the black and blue under his eyes revealed his exhaustion from a sleepless night; Liu Jiaqi's face was delicate, and there was a trace of unnoticeable vigilance in her eyes, but she did not look like a criminal.
"You said you were doing small business in other places, what exactly did you do?" Officer Wang's voice slowed down a little, "Where did you do it? Is there anyone you know who can prove it?"
"Opened a Chinese restaurant." Ling Feng answered quickly. This was the area he was most familiar with. "In... a small county in the south, called Xikou. There are a lot of acquaintances there, but we haven't had much contact in the past few years. If we suddenly go there, I'm afraid they won't remember it." He deliberately mentioned a remote place name, betting that the other party would not check it immediately.
Officer Wang tapped his fingertips on the keyboard, and relevant information about Xikou County popped up on the screen. He looked at it for a few seconds, then raised his eyes and said: "Xikou County completed electronic identity registration for all employees five years ago. Even if you left ten years ago, there should be original household registration files in the system. But now, your information is completely blank, just like..." He paused and did not continue, but the inquiry in his eyes was already obvious.
Liu Jiaqi's heart was in her throat, and she subconsciously held Ling Feng's hand. Ling Feng felt the coldness in her palm and gently shook it back, signaling her not to panic. He knew that blindly emphasizing "lost documents" was no longer tenable, and he had to think of a more reasonable explanation.
"Officer," Ling Feng's tone was serious, as if he had made up his mind, "To tell you the truth, we have not had a smooth life in the past ten years. Something happened in the middle and we lost contact with our family. Later, we changed jobs several times, and our living place was not fixed. Even the original one I almost forgot the name... I came to Shanghai this time just to start over, but I didn’t expect that I got lost as soon as I arrived.” He was deliberately vague, citing the reason for “lost documents” as “out of touch with society”, trying to explain the abnormality of information blankness with a sense of abjection.
This statement is half true and half false, but it just hits some possible social phenomena. Officer Wang's brows relaxed a little. He had seen many people who deliberately "disappeared" to avoid debts and family conflicts. Although the two people in front of him did not look alike, this possibility could not be completely ruled out.
He was silent for a moment, then stood up and said, "You guys wait here for a moment, I'll report the situation to the leader."
The office door was gently closed, and only Ling Feng and Liu Jiaqi were left in the reception room. The air seemed to be frozen, and only the electronic clock on the wall was beating silently, and every second seemed to hit my heart.
"A Feng," Liu Jiaqi's voice was low and trembling, "will they... doubt us?"
Ling Feng held her hand and conveyed the warmth from his fingertips: "Don't worry, we didn't do anything wrong, it's just that our status is a bit special. At most, they think we are out-of-contact people and won't think about other places." Even so, he didn't know for sure. Will police officers in this era have sharper intuition? Are there any flaws in their words and deeds?
